title: Portable EV Charger vs Home EV Charger: Which One Do You Actually Need?
summary: Compare portable EV chargers and wall-mounted home EV chargers. Explore 3.3 kW, 7.4 kW, 11 kW and 22 kW options to find the right setup.
body_markdown:
You park your EV at home every night. A wall-mounted charger sounds convenient. Then you remember the trips you take, the relatives you visit, and the days when your car isn’t parked in its usual spot.


Now a portable EV charger starts to make sense.


The choice isn’t simply between a cheaper option and a more powerful one. A portable charger gives you flexibility. A wall-mounted home EV charger gives you a dedicated charging point for your everyday routine.


Neither setup suits everyone. Your parking arrangement, electrical supply and charging habits matter more than the product category alone.


Statiq offers both:[Flow portable EV chargers](https://www.statiq.in/3.3kw) for flexible charging and[Nectar wall-mounted chargers](https://www.statiq.in/nectar) for a dedicated home setup.


## **Portable EV Charger vs Home EV Charger: A Quick Comparison**


Both ranges use a Type 2 AC vehicle connector. The input connection and installation requirements are different, so check those before choosing.


## **1. Portable Charging: Useful When Your Parking Spot Changes**


Think about where your car spends its time.


If you rent your home, travel between properties, or occasionally park somewhere other than your usual spot, a portable car charger for an EV gives you more flexibility. You can carry it with you instead of depending entirely on one fixed charging point.


A portable EV charger is worth considering if you:


- **Live in a rented property:** You can take the charger with you when you move, without leaving a permanently installed charging unit behind.
- **Travel frequently:** A compatible power connection at your destination gives you another charging option.
- **Want a backup:** Keep the charger in your car for situations where your regular charging arrangement isn’t available.
- **Need a flexible home setup:** Use it at home if you have a suitable socket and electrical supply.
- **Don’t want permanent installation:** You can avoid installing a fixed wallbox, provided the available connection is appropriate for the charger.


### **Which Statiq Flow Portable Charger Should You Consider?**

**Statiq Flow 3.3 kW portable EV charger**

It is the lower-powered option in the range. Before using it, check that the socket is suitable for the charger’s specified current and that your EV supports Type 2 AC charging.


**Statiq Flow 7.4 kW portable EV charger**


The higher-output variant offers more current-adjustment flexibility and a display with additional charging information.

- Vehicle connector: Type 2 AC

- Timer: Charging can be scheduled up to 12 hours in advance


This model supports the specified 5/3-pin industrial input plug arrangement, with 3-pin M-type compatibility as described in its product specifications. Check the exact variant and input connection before ordering.


The available socket and electrical supply must support the intended charging current. Choosing the higher rating alone doesn’t guarantee faster charging. Compare the[Statiq Flow portable EV charger](https://www.statiq.in/shop/flow-portable-ev-charger) options to find a variant that suits your charging requirements.


## **2. Wall-Mounted Charging: Better Suited to a Fixed Home Setup**


If you park in the same place every night, a wall-mounted EV charger can be the more convenient arrangement. The charging unit stays installed near your parking space, ready for regular use.


You don’t need to take the charger out of the boot, connect it to a separate socket and pack it away after each session.


A fixed home charger is worth considering if you have dedicated parking, charge frequently at home and want connected charging controls. Installation requires a suitable location and an assessment of the property’s electrical supply.


### **Statiq Nectar Home EV Charger Options**


Nectar is Statiq’s wall-mounted home charging range. It comes in three power configurations.


**Charger** **Power supply** **Best fit**


7.4 kW Single-phase Everyday or overnight home charging


11 kW Three-phase Regular charging where a higher output is required


22 kW Three-phase Higher charging demand, where the home supply and vehicle support it


The higher ratings are not automatically better for every household. Your vehicle’s onboard AC charger limits how much power it can accept, and your home’s electrical supply must support the selected charger.


Nectar also includes connected features for managing home charging:


- **Statiq App controls:** View, schedule and track charging sessions.
- **Dynamic load management:** Balances power use to help prevent the home’s electrical supply from becoming overloaded.
- **Automatic cut-off:** Stops power when charging is complete.
- **Electrical and thermal protection:** Supports stable operation during charging.
- **Indoor and outdoor suitability:** The product specifies IP66 and IK10 protection.


A professional site assessment helps establish the right installation arrangement. Cable routing, electrical capacity and the location of the parking space all need consideration. Check the[Statiq Nectar home EV chargers](https://www.statiq.in/shop/nectar-home-ev-charger) to compare the available power configurations and connected charging features.


## **4. 3.3 kW vs 7.4 kW vs 11 kW vs 22 kW: Which Power Level Should You Choose?**


These numbers describe maximum charging output, not a guaranteed charging speed for every EV.


**Power option** **Charger type** **What to check before choosing**


3.3 kW Portable Compatible 3-pin connection, current requirements and vehicle support


7.4 kW Portable or wall-mounted Suitable power supply, input connection and vehicle’s AC charging capacity


11 kW Wall-mounted Three-phase supply and compatible onboard charger


22 kW Wall-mounted Adequate three-phase capacity and vehicle support for the higher output


A 22 kW home charger won’t necessarily charge your car at 22 kW. If your EV supports a lower maximum AC charging rate, that limit still applies.


The same principle works in reverse. Buying a portable charger with a higher maximum output won’t help if the power connection can’t safely support it.


Before buying, check your EV’s specifications and your property’s electrical capacity together. Looking at either one in isolation can lead to the wrong choice.


## **4. Can a Portable EV Charger Handle Everyday Home Charging?**


It can, provided the charger, power connection and vehicle are suitable for regular use.


A portable EV charger doesn’t have to be reserved for emergencies or road trips. If you have a suitable socket near your parking space, it can be used for home charging without permanently mounting the charging unit.


The trade-off is convenience. You’ll handle the charger and cable for each session, while a wall-mounted unit stays in place and is ready to connect.


If you want regular home charging alongside app-based session monitoring, scheduling and load management, Nectar is the more relevant option to explore.


You can also use both setups for different purposes: Nectar for your usual home charging and Flow as a portable option for travel or backup. That arrangement makes sense for drivers who value a dedicated home setup but don’t want to depend on it exclusively.


## **5. Check These Details Before Placing Your Order**


The product specifications deserve a closer look before you decide.


**Your vehicle’s connector and charging capacity**


Confirm that your EV supports Type 2 AC charging. Check its maximum AC charging rate too; this helps you choose a charger with a suitable output.


**The socket or electrical supply**


For a portable model, confirm the input plug type and the electrical supply requirements. For a wall-mounted charger, check whether your home has the necessary single-phase or three-phase supply.


**The installation location**


A fixed charger needs a suitable position near the parking space. The installer should assess cable routing, wiring and electrical protection before installation.


**Safety requirements**


Use an appropriate power connection and follow the product’s instructions. Avoid improvised connections, unsuitable adapters and extension cords. Have the electrical arrangement assessed rather than assuming an existing socket is suitable.


**The exact product variant**


The Statiq 7.4 kW portable charger is offered with or without the industrial plug. Confirm which version you’re purchasing and what the package includes.


These checks are more useful than choosing a charger based on its power rating alone.


## **Which Statiq EV Charger Is Right for You?**


If your parking location changes, you rent your home, or you want a charging option for travel, **Statiq Flow** is the range to consider. Its 3.3 kW and 7.4 kW variants offer different output ratings and input arrangements.


If your EV stays in dedicated home parking and you want a fixed charging point, **Statiq Nectar** offers 7.4 kW, 11 kW and 22 kW options, along with connected charging controls.


Start with your vehicle, parking arrangement and electrical supply. Once those are clear, choosing between portable and wall-mounted charging becomes much easier.


## **FAQs**


**1. What is the main difference between a portable EV charger and a home wallbox?**


A portable charger can be carried between suitable locations and doesn’t need permanent wall mounting. A wallbox is installed at a dedicated charging location for regular use.


**2. Can I use a 7.4 kW portable EV charger at home?**


Yes, if the vehicle, electrical supply and compatible input connection meet the charger’s requirements. Confirm these details before using it.


**3. Should I choose an 11 kW or 22 kW home EV charger?**


Check your EV’s maximum AC charging capacity and your home’s three-phase electrical supply. The higher rating is useful only if the complete setup supports it.


**4. Does a portable EV charger need professional installation?**


It doesn’t require permanent wall mounting, but the power connection still needs to be suitable and safe. Have the electrical supply checked if you’re unsure about its capacity or condition.


**5. Can I keep a portable charger as a backup if I have a wallbox?**


Yes. A portable charger can provide another charging option when you’re away from home or your usual charging arrangement isn’t available, provided a compatible power connection is accessible.
